evidence: bogus-packets-are-sent: baseline :159-160 (rule 501, ctstate INVALID in mangle PREROUTING) and :162-163 (502) are what the follow-up check the-invalid-and-not-syn-rules-dropped-them reads; this setup step only proves hping3 sent 5 SYN+FIN, 50 RST and 5 stray ACKs (its expect is the send count, the rule effect is judged in the next check from rule 501/502 counters), consistent with the lines

the-rst-limit-dropped-the-third: baseline :187-190 declare rule 519 accept RST at limit 2/sec burst 2 and 520 drop the rest, so 3 simultaneous RSTs -> 2 accepted, 1 dropped is what those lines declare; the class's own rule 003 (:119-123, accept RELATED,ESTABLISHED, sorted before 519) takes in-connection RSTs and rule 501 drops out-of-connection ones as INVALID, so the declared limit is unreachable - the check correctly tests the declared outcome and its failure is a finding, not a derivation error

policies-and-ssh-rules: baseline :83-84 set INPUT and FORWARD policy drop (OUTPUT untouched, ACCEPT), :135-137 one '100 SSH whitelist' rule per entry of unique(flatten(lab Hiera whitelist + fixture acl)) = 2, and :153 rule 116 in LIMIT_OVERALL for strict=false; the probe reads exactly those with iptables -S

finding the-rst-limit-dropped-the-third: the node's counters for rule 519 and 520 rose by 0 and 0 after the peer reset 3 connections at once (expected 2 and 1): the RSTs never reach rules 519/520 (rule 003 accepts ESTABLISHED first) - same unreachable RST limit the set itself names in its fragment row

finding held-ssh-connections-stop-at-eight: the peer saw 7 established SSH connections (expected 8) after 10 connections one every 4 s held by timeout 50 nc; baseline :130/:149 (connlimit_above 8) allow up to 8, so one of the first 8 was not held: either a dropped or closed connection (e.g. sshd ending an unauthenticated nc session) or a real limit below 8; the author's run passed this check, so the two runs disagree and the check's exact-8 expectation is not reproducible as written

purpose covered: Purpose (default-drop + SSH brute-force limits + DDoS extras + whitelist side chain + blacklist) matches the header (:1-13) and code. Tested on the applied node with a peer: policies and SSH rules, loopback accept (001), the three SSH limits (overall 20/min burst 5, 8 held, 15 new/min), mangle drops 501/502/503 by counters, ICMP 2/sec limit, the RST limit (a finding: unreachable), whitelist-only access to the service through the side chain with its connlimit and new-connection rate, the blacklist dropping every protocol (local change #5) while an unlisted source passes, purge of unmanaged rules at the next agent run, and the flush script plus rebuild. Uncovered rows are true: rule 002 and rule 518 measured inert (defrag runs before mangle; 127/8 destination dropped before INPUT), geoip needs xtables-addons and a GeoIP DB, internal_forward needs an internal network, and the no-ip_filter / no-anti_ddos / strict variants need another fixture of the same node (one set holds one fixture). Minor: rows 002 and 518 name lifted_by ubuntu although their reasons say no node would show the rule act; compile-time fail() validations (:39-52) are not rows (no node outcome).
